title: What to make, and what it meets

blocks.text: Eleven things you can ask for and six of them are not living artefacts. Your skills mostly stack on top of this runtime rather than compete with it; two genuinely collide, and one of those is the likeliest source of the next mess. Pin a note on any row.

blocks.info: The question that picks the row is what the thing is for, never what it looks like.

blocks.info: Five tensions. Two are real conflicts, three only look like one until the rule is written down.

head: Tension
What goes wrong
What I do unless you say otherwise
rows: two ways to publish a Verbolia PRD, both tabbed, both editable, both on brand. Whichever I pick, the other one rots
use this repo. `verbolia-prd` predates the fused form. D-1 settles it
Claude Docs against a living artefact
both are "a living document". Docs wins on co-editing and comment threads; this wins on the typed journal and the templates
a living artefact when it is you and me over rounds, a Doc when more than one person writes. D-2
reaching for brand tokens to style a document breaks the rule the whole runtime rests on
add what is missing to the runtime, never to a document
that skill assumes a separate static copy per audience; the fused form says there is one page
one page inside Verbolia, a static copy only to leave it
looks like a contradiction: one artefact per component, but one increment per turn
no conflict. One component per artefact, one section per turn, inside the same artefact

blocks.info: Three decisions. D-1 is the one that prevents the next mess.

head: Decision
Why it matters
rows: Retire `verbolia-prd`, or keep it and point it at this runtime?
two vessels for the same document is the likeliest way to end up with a mess again. Retiring it is one edit to its description
What is this runtime for, now that Claude Docs exists?
carried from the last round unanswered. It decides what gets built after the Publish button
Does the Publish button's changelog live in the model, or only in the page?
in the model it is content you can edit and I can read back; in the page it is a view that costs nothing and survives nothing
